response.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS account_count FROM account GROUP BY district_id), totals AS (SELECT SUM(account_count) AS total_accounts FROM counts), shares AS (SELECT c.district_id, c.account_count, CAST(c.account_count AS REAL) / t.total_accounts AS share FROM counts c CROSS JOIN totals t), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares), diffs AS (SELECT s.district_id, s.account_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS share_diff FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a), ranked AS (SELECT d.*, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY d.share_diff DESC) AS rnk FROM diffs d) SELECT district_id, account_count, share, share_diff FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY share_diff DESC;

assumptions.assumption: account.district_id is the branch district for each account, and each row in account is one account, so COUNT(*) per district_id gives the account count. The total is the sum of those counts, which equals the number of rows in account.

The average share is taken across the districts that have at least one account (the grouped districts), not across all 77 rows of the district table. Districts with zero accounts are excluded from the average.
RANK() on share_diff keeps every district tied with the 10th, so the output can exceed 10 rows. Ties are exact equality of the computed floating-point difference. No rounding is applied.

alternatives.interpretation: Average share is taken across all districts in the district table, with districts that have no accounts counted as share 0. The average is then the total of the shares divided by the number of district rows, not by the number of districts that have accounts.
alternatives.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS account_count FROM account GROUP BY district_id), total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_accounts FROM account), all_d AS (SELECT d.district_id, COALESCE(c.account_count, 0) AS account_count, CAST(COALESCE(c.account_count, 0) AS REAL) / (SELECT total_accounts FROM total) AS share FROM district d LEFT JOIN counts c ON c.district_id = d.district_id), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM all_d), diffs AS (SELECT a.district_id, a.account_count, a.share, a.share - v.avg_share AS share_diff FROM all_d a CROSS JOIN avg_share v), ranked AS (SELECT d.*, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY d.share_diff DESC) AS rnk FROM diffs d) SELECT district_id, account_count, share, share_diff FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY share_diff DESC;
